extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, students of literature, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: A compact set of evaluative principles for writing and assessing literature, distilled from Italo Calvino's 'Six Memos for the Next Millennium' (lightness, quickness, exactitude, visibility, multiplicity, and an unwritten consistency). Meant to guide craft decisions and critical judgment about fiction's aims and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lightness
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have tried to remove weight, sometimes from people, sometimes from heavenly bodies, sometimes from cities; above all, I have tried to remove weight from the structure of stories and from language." Lightness as a literary quality is not frivolousness but a way of rising above the noise of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightness permits treatment of serious themes without heaviness; it involves stripping excess weight from narrative structures and language. Examples cited: Cavalcanti's poetry, Kundera's The Unbearable Lightness of Being. Diagnostic question from the memos: Is the work light without being trivial? Avoid the anti-pattern of equating seriousness with density or overwrought solemnity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quickness
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of narrative compression: the ability to compress vast experience into a few words so that every word counts toward the speed of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickness is a discipline of craft—economy of structure and diction—modeled on folktales and short forms. Practical guidance: eliminate verbal padding, sharpen pacing so essential moments register with immediacy. Diagnostic question: Is the work quick in its essential moments? Anti-patterns include unnecessary discursiveness and diffuse pacing that dissipate narrative momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactitude comprises three primary aspects: (1) a well-defined and well-calculated plan for the work; (2) evocation of clear, incisive, memorable visual images; (3) a language as precise as possible both in choice of words and in expression of subtleties of thought and imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both macro-precision (architectural clarity, deliberate structure) and micro-precision (word choice, nuance). Examples: precision in plotting, in imagery, and in linguistic nuance. Diagnostic question: Is the work exact — both architecturally and word-by-word? Anti-patterns: vague plotting, fuzzy imagery, imprecise diction that blunts meaning or emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'visual imagination'—the writer's ability to make the reader see: mental images are made of words; the writer must select words that conjure pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize sensory, image-driven writing so the reader perceives scenes and details. Calvino warns that this faculty is endangered by media saturation, so deliberate evocation of sight (and other senses) is a corrective. Diagnostic question: Does the work make the reader see? Anti-patterns: relying on summary or abstract discussion instead of concrete imagery; assuming media visuals substitute for verbal description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel as multiple worlds, multiple perspectives, multiple knowledge systems woven together; a great work holds multiplicities without collapsing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design works to accommodate plural viewpoints, narrative layers, and heterogenous knowledge without forcing artificial unification. Examples: Borges, Perec, Calvino's Invisible Cities. Diagnostic question: Does the work hold multiplicity without dissolving? Anti-patterns: flattening distinct voices into one homogenous perspective or attempting a false, simplistic synthesis that erases tension among systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency (unwritten/mended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calvino did not complete the sixth memo; speculation suggests he intended to treat the way a great work coheres despite (or via) multiplicity—i.e., consistency or coherence across a work's parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work achieves coherence (formal, thematic, tonal) even while practicing multiplicity, lightness, quickness, etc. Consider how recurring patterns, structures, or ethical/imaginal commitments bind disparate elements. Diagnostic question (inferred): Does the work cohere without collapsing its pluralities? Anti-patterns: incoherence that feels accidental rather than artful; forced uniformity that negates productive multiplicity.
